Task name: Aurelian Skin - Ecommerce skincare image system
Sector: Clinical skincare and personal care, actives-led, direct to consumer plus specialty retail
Founded / place / size: Founded 2024 in Boston, Massachusetts. A two person founder team, sold for a year to a waiting list and through two dermatology practices before the retail season.
About: Aurelian Skin is a small clinical skincare line built on eight actives-led products at thirty four to sixty eight dollars. In March we open our own online store and enter a specialty chain's twelve doors, so everything a customer sees changes at once. The line is meant to read like a laboratory with good taste: cool, quiet, evidence first, generous with white space and free of decoration. Not a spa, not a discount aisle. Our customer reads the ingredient list before the copy, and the brand is built to reward that: honest claims, clear INCI, restraint in place of ritual.
Audience: Women roughly twenty six to forty two, ingredient literate, who research formulations and trust plainness over promise. They shop web stores and specialty beauty floors and judge a product by its panel.
Price positioning: Prestige-mass at thirty four to sixty eight dollars per SKU. Above the mass aisle, below luxury conserve pricing. The middle is the position, and the look must not drift warm and cheap or dark and precious.
Personality: Clinical, Precise, Restrained, Evidence-led, Understated
Palette:
Clinical White #F4F6F7 · mandatory. The ground of every designed surface: the product-page modules, the key visual's type area and every carousel page, and the white space the brand is generous with.
Graphite #232729 · mandatory. Type (product names, claims, body, INCI and prices) and the 0.5 pt hairline under every product name. Never a ground or a panel.
Cool Mineral Grey #9BA5AA · optional accent. Keylines, such as the keyline around an INCI panel, and small labels such as the INCI heading. Never a ground, never body text.
Signal Blue #3E6076 · optional accent. Thin rules and dividers only. Never the hairline under a product name, which is Graphite, never a ground, never body text.
Typography: Aurelian Skin runs four steps on screen. Step 01 is the product name in Signifier Light at 44 px on 48 px leading, set in capitals and tracked to 340 units, with a 0.5 pt Graphite hairline ruled beneath to the exact measure of the name. Step 02 is the cleared claim, also Signifier Light, at 24 px on 28 px with tracking of minus 6 units, sitting under the hairline and always reading quieter than the name. Step 03 is body in Söhne Buch 400 at 15 px on 22 px, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters a line. Step 04 is fine print in Söhne Mono 400 at 11 px on 16 px with tracking of plus 12 units and tabular lining figures, carrying INCI, percentages and prices, with the on-screen price set in the same mono at 28 px. In print the carton name is 15 pt and the INCI panel 6.5 pt. The wordmark is never rebuilt in a sans.
Signature type move: Product names are always Signifier Light capitals tracked to 340 units, sitting on a 0.5 pt Graphite hairline ruled to the exact measure of the name and nothing wider.
Voice: Measured, factual, unhurried. States what a product does and does not claim. Reads like a well-run lab that respects the reader, never breathless and never coy.
Values: Ingredient honesty, precision in every detail from panel to package, and clinical restraint: at this band, quiet and exact is the brand, and overstatement or gloss would undercut the claim.
Brand assets status: The original logo file was lost when the first designer's drive failed. All that survives is a handheld photograph of an outer carton showing the mark printed in one deep ink: a small-caps lockup set around a monogram, separated by a hairline rule. Recovering that mark as usable artwork is part of this engagement. No other source brand files remain.
Palette rules:
Distribution: Every flat, non-photographic ground and panel is Clinical White. All type is Graphite, set on Clinical White or on a photograph's own pale sweep, apart from a small label such as the INCI heading, which may be Cool Mineral Grey. Cool Mineral Grey and Signal Blue are accents for keylines, rules and small labels, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground and never body text.
Opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, drop shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph; type sits on Clinical White or on the photograph's own pale sweep.
Forbidden: No gold, bronze, silver or other metallic or gloss effect, no warm tint and no dark or near-black ground in the designed areas, since the look must not drift warm and cheap or dark and precious, and no colour outside the four palette hexes for type, grounds, panels, rules, buttons or icons.
Photography: Photographs keep their own true, corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette. The amber glass of aurelian_launch_shoot_01.jpg and aurelian_launch_shoot_04.jpg and the golden retinol drop and black ground of aurelian_actives_macro_04.jpg stay as shot; the no-gold and no-dark-ground rules govern designed elements only. The cool cast of aurelian_launch_shoot_02.jpg and aurelian_launch_shoot_05.jpg is corrected to neutral, never kept or pushed toward Signal Blue.

Task name: Corner & Cure - Spring dish launch photography

Burnt Butter #B8823A · optional accent. The hairline rule between the allergen line and the provenance line, as on last spring's card. Never type, never a ground.
Scrubbed Oak #C9B79C · optional accent. Hairline rules and dividers only. Never type, never a ground.

Sector: Boutique residential real estate brokerage specialising in architect-designed listings, residential property in Marin County.

We present listings the way the architecture asks to be seen: quietly, accurately, and next to whatever three other agents are showing. Our credibility rests on buyers and vendors trusting that the pictures are the house.
Audience: Buyers aged 40 to 60 with household incomes above 400 thousand who read light and material as proxies for build quality, and vendors of design-led homes. They view our listings alongside three competing agents and notice anything that looks retouched.
Price positioning: High-value residential, flagship listings from the low millions up. Positioned above volume agencies and apart from developer marketing, on restraint and accuracy rather than gloss.
Personality: restrained, precise, cool, credible, understated, considered

Plaster White #F2F1ED · mandatory. The solid ground of every brochure page and of every panel or margin that carries type on the portal hero and room posts, as on windowcard_2025_print.pdf.
Marin Slate #3C444B · mandatory where body text appears. Body text on Plaster White, as the body on windowcard_2025_print.pdf; may also carry the spec table, the price and fine print. Never a ground or panel.
Deep Charcoal #1E2124 · mandatory. The stacked address, on Plaster White, as the address on windowcard_2025_print.pdf; may also carry headings, the price and the enquiry line. Never a ground or panel.
Bay Grey #7E8A8C · optional accent. Hairline rules and dividers only, as on windowcard_2025_print.pdf. Never a ground, panel or type colour.

Warm Stone #C7B9A4 · optional accent. A small accent only, such as a key line or a small mark. Never a ground, panel or type colour, so nothing reads warm and cosy.

Step 02 is the standfirst, also Tobias Light, at 13 pt on 17 pt with tracking of minus 2 units. Step 03 is body in Neue Haas Grotesk Text 55 Roman at 9.5 pt on 14 pt, tracking 0, held to a maximum of 65 characters. Step 04 is the spec table and price in the same grotesque at 8 pt on 11 pt with tracking of plus 8 units and tabular lining figures. On screen the room post address runs 56 px and the enquiry line 24 px. A price is never set in Tobias.
Signature type move: Every address is stacked, the street number alone above the street name in Tobias Light, flush left, unpunctuated and never italic.
Voice: Cool, restrained and true. We describe what is there and let the room speak. No superlatives, no cosiness, nothing that sounds sold. Example line: 'Glass on three sides, the bay through the living room, the oaks off the kitchen.'

Brand assets status: There is no working design source for the office window cards. The feature sheet and portal module are expected to be handed back as editable documents because prices move.

Bay Grey is for hairline rules and dividers only; Quiet Sage and Warm Stone are small accents only. Bay Grey, Quiet Sage and Warm Stone together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground, a panel or a type colour.
Opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, no type carries a drop shadow or glow, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: type sits on a solid Plaster White block beside or over the photograph.
Forbidden: No gold, brass, bronze or other metallic colour or effect on any type, panel, rule, button or icon, and no black-and-gold treatment: the office rules out developer gold-and-black. No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons.
Photography: Photographs keep their own corrected, neutral colour and are never recoloured toward the palette. Cool does not mean blue: plaster whites stay neutral, blacks keep their detail, grass keeps its own green, and every sky and window view is the one captured in its frame, never dropped in. The colour prohibitions govern the design, not the photographs: the teak cladding and door of room_12.jpg and the steel range and tap of room_02.jpg stay as shot.

Sector: Mid-premium homeware: glazed stoneware and woven textiles
Founded / place / size: Founded in Providence, Rhode Island. A two-person workshop selling direct to consumer and wholesale into fourteen independent stores across the Northeast.
About: Thornmere Home makes glazed stoneware and woven textiles in a small Providence workshop, with around thirty-two products a season priced from forty-five to a hundred and eighty dollars. Real glaze, dye and texture are central to the work. Ceramics are photographed standing and textiles draped, so the range feels warm and related without disguising the individual objects. This commission focuses on twenty pieces from the autumn range.
Audience: Buyers roughly thirty to fifty who nest and furnish slowly. Design literate, buying to keep rather than to chase a trend. Neither farmhouse cliche nor design-gallery cool, just people who want warm, made things in the house.
Price positioning: Mid-premium. Generous with white space, warm and truthful about material, never the austere near-black of collectible ceramics and never the crowded, saturated look of discount homeware.
Personality: Quiet, Warm, Honest, Handmade, Unfussy

Task name: Fennhollow - Botanical soda summer campaign
Tagline: Botanicals from the valley, nothing else.
Sector: Craft botanical soda, better-for-you premium CPG
Founded / place / size: Founded in the Hudson Valley, New York. Two founders working with a co-packer, three flavours, sold in upstate natural grocers and by direct-to-consumer subscription.
About: Fennhollow Botanical Soda makes three botanical sodas in the Hudson Valley: elderflower and lime, rhubarb and bitters, and spruce tip. Three dollars fifty a can, sold across upstate natural grocers and by subscription, produced through a co-packer whose cleared nutrition claim cannot be reworded. Two founders run everything and neither is a photographer. The whole brand lives on summer: sun lit, warm, natural, a little restrained. The spruce tip flavour steps to the front in August, so the summer campaign has to be built to be revisited as the season shifts.
Audience: Twenty-five to forty, shopping the natural grocer aisle and reading the ingredient panel. Paying a premium for the promise that this is closer to a real thing than a mass soda.
Price positioning: Craft better-for-you at three fifty a can. Warmer and more human than a twelve-dollar apothecary tonic, and far more restrained and natural than a hyper-saturated ninety-nine-cent soda.
Personality: Sun lit, Natural, Restrained, Warm, Made by real people
Palette:
Label Green #3F6B3A · mandatory. Every flavour name set on Warm Cream Ground or over a light part of a photograph, as fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf sets its flavour name and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf its title; the half point rule that splits every stacked flavour name; the co-packer's claim line may be Label Green, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. It is the only solid panel colour besides Warm Cream Ground.
Warm Cream Ground #F4ECD8 · mandatory. The main ground of every designed area, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf, and all type set on a Label Green panel.
Afternoon Amber #E5AF54 · optional accent. A small price tag device with the price figure reversed out of it, as the price flag on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. Never a ground, panel, rule or type colour.
Rhubarb Rose #C56E68 · optional accent. Small letterspaced labels and the short thin rule set just above them, as the NOW POURING label and its rule on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. Never a ground, panel or body text.
Deep Ink #2C2A24 · mandatory where body text sits on Warm Cream Ground. Body text, subheads, fine print and the sourcing line on Warm Cream Ground, as fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf sets its store name and sourcing line and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf its body. Never a ground or panel.
Typography: Fennhollow Botanical Soda runs four steps. Step 01, Display and H1, is Staatliches Regular caps at 120 pt on 108 pt leading, tracked -5 thousandths, set as the poster flavour name stacked onto two centred lines split by a half point rule in Label Green. Step 02, Subheading and H2, is Staatliches Regular caps at 96 px on 104 px, tracked -5 thousandths, for the key visual headline, stepping down to 64 px on 70 px on a carousel page and still stacked on two centred lines. Step 03, Body, is Whitney Book at 30 px on 42 px, tracking 0, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, with Whitney Semibold at the same size for subheads. Step 04, Fine print, is Whitney Book at 18 pt on 24 pt, tracked +15 thousandths, and it carries the co-packer's cleared claim line exactly as written. A flavour name is never set on a single line.
Signature type move: Every flavour name stacks onto two centred lines of Staatliches caps split by a half point rule in Label Green, so the stacked block registers before the words are read.
Voice: Plain, warm, a little rural. Names the botanicals and the valley, not a lifestyle. The co-packer's cleared claim line stays exactly as written.
Values: Real ingredients over additives, provable and legal image provenance the co-packer can be shown, and a cohesive look the next hire can build on rather than start from nothing.
Brand assets status: No written brand guidelines have ever existed and the founders asked for the first one to be created. Their brand note points to a printed swatch card that was never sent with the package, so the house green survives only as the printed label on the two studio can shots the brand owns. There is no lifestyle photography of any kind.
Palette rules:
Distribution: Grounds and panels are Warm Cream Ground or Label Green and nothing else; Warm Cream Ground is the main ground, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf and fennhollow_brand_note.pdf. On Warm Cream Ground, flavour names and their half point rules are Label Green, and body text, subheads and fine print are Deep Ink; the co-packer's claim line may be Deep Ink or Label Green, as on fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf. A stacked flavour name never sits on a Label Green panel, where its rule would vanish. On a Label Green panel all type is Warm Cream Ground, as the can labels in fennhollow_packshot_01.jpg and fennhollow_packshot_02.jpg set pale type on the green. Type set directly over a photograph, which fennhollow_brand_note.pdf expects, is Deep Ink or Label Green over light areas and Warm Cream Ground over dark ones. Afternoon Amber is for a small price tag and Rhubarb Rose for small labels and thin rules; together they cover no more than 10% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground, a panel or body text.
Opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour or to type, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: type sits directly on the photograph or on a solid block. The one tint is a thin Label Green rule above the fine print at 45% opacity, as fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf sets its foot rule, and nowhere else.
Forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes (#3F6B3A, #F4ECD8, #E5AF54, #C56E68 and #2C2A24) for type, grounds, panels, rules, buttons or icons, with three exceptions carried from fennhollow_shelftalker_press.pdf: a price figure reversed out of an Afternoon Amber tag may be white, a town line under a store name may be the warm grey #57534A, and the one 45% Label Green rule above the fine print allowed under opacity reads as its tint. No neon or hyper-saturated colour and no glow anywhere in the design, which the brand places against a hyper-saturated ninety-nine-cent soda.
Photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette; the can's aluminium stays silver. The one exception is the printed can label: our green is the label green, and it must still read as our Label Green through every correction.

Task name: Cape Marren - Shoulder-season tourism campaign
Sector: Regional destination marketing, an alliance of independent coastal member businesses
Founded / place / size: A visitor alliance of twenty two independent member businesses along the Cape Marren coast on the North American Atlantic seaboard. Coordinated by Nell on behalf of the members. Small, member funded, regional in reach.
About: Cape Marren Coast Alliance markets a stretch of independent coast to shoulder season visitors. Summer sells itself; the work is October to April, when a harbour seafood room, a cider barn, a point light, a bookshop, a bakery and an oyster landing either make a living or do not. The campaign has to feel like that season honestly: warm low sun, weather, wool, wet stone, a lit window at four in the afternoon, quiet compositions with one or two people. Members have to see themselves in it, because members who cannot see themselves do not renew.
Audience: Travellers aged 30 to 60, driving from within four hours, mostly couples and pairs of friends rather than families. They spend 200 to 600 dollars per party across a two or three night shoulder season weekend on rooms, meals, cider and a walk.
Price positioning: Mid range and real. Positioned above a peak summer holiday treatment (which would oversell blue water and hard sun) and below a 1,500 dollar luxury coastal weekend (which would go near monochrome and strand the bakery and the cider barn). Editorial rather than promotional, and never promising a season the coast cannot deliver in November.
Personality: Honest, Warm, Grounded, Understated, Weathered
Palette:
Warm October Sun #C8894B · mandatory wherever an Anton headline appears. The single 3 pt rule locked beneath every Anton headline at the headline's exact width, other hairline rules, and trail numbers, as the rule and the trail number on trailcard_2025_print.pdf. Never a ground, a panel, a headline or body text.
Wet Stone #5B5F5C · optional accent. Small secondary type on Wool Cream only: labels, captions and contact lines, as the trail label and contact line on trailcard_2025_print.pdf and the COAST ALLIANCE line of alliance_mark.svg. Never a ground, a panel, a headline or body text.
Wool Cream #E7DDC9 · mandatory. The main ground, as on trailcard_2025_print.pdf, a solid light panel, and all type set on a Deep Harbour panel.
Deep Harbour #2E3A3C · mandatory. Headlines, member names, body text and opening months on Wool Cream, as on trailcard_2025_print.pdf; the alliance mark's drawing and CAPE MARREN lettering; and the only dark solid panel, which then carries Wool Cream type.
Typography: Cape Marren Coast Alliance runs four steps. Step 01, Display and H1, is Anton Regular caps at 180 pt on 168 pt leading, tracking 0 because Anton is never letterspaced, with a single Warm October Sun rule of 3 pt locked directly beneath at the headline's exact width. Step 02, Subheading and H2, is Anton Regular caps at 42 pt on 46 pt, tracking 0, for a member feature, with the same 3 pt rule beneath; a carousel page runs 64 px on 62 px, and the 46 pt leading was invented because the prose states none. Step 03, Body, is Atlas Grotesk Regular at 10.5 pt on 15 pt, tracking 0, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters. Step 04, Fine print, is Atlas Grotesk Regular at 11 pt on 15 pt, tracked +15 thousandths, and it carries captions, member names and trail numbers, 11 pt in print or 28 px on screen, with Atlas Grotesk Medium tabular figures for opening months. Anton is never letterspaced.
Signature type move: Every headline is Anton caps sitting on a single Warm October Sun rule of 3 pt locked directly beneath it at the headline's exact width, so the eye catches a heavy block of type resting on one orange bar.
Voice: Grounded and truthful. Warm about the place without overselling it, and specific about what a visitor will actually find when they arrive out of season.
Values: Honesty about the season, keeping every member visible, and supporting the independent businesses that fund the alliance.
Brand assets status: No written brand guidelines exist. The only brand file on hand is the alliance mark left by the previous agency, supplied as a single vector file with nothing else: no color system, no type list and no usage notes. Members submit their own photographs and object shots, and the campaign look is set by this brief rather than by any existing kit.
Palette rules:
Distribution: Grounds are Wool Cream, and a solid panel is Wool Cream or Deep Harbour, nothing else. On Wool Cream, headlines, member names, body text and opening months are Deep Harbour, and small labels, captions and contact lines are Deep Harbour or Wet Stone, as on trailcard_2025_print.pdf. On Deep Harbour, all type is Wool Cream. Type set directly on a photograph is Wool Cream or Deep Harbour. Warm October Sun is only for the 3 pt rule beneath each Anton headline, other hairline rules and trail numbers; Warm October Sun and Wet Stone together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area.
Opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: type sits on a clear area of the photograph or on a solid panel.
Forbidden: No colour outside #C8894B, #5B5F5C, #E7DDC9 and #2E3A3C for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons. No summer blue or turquoise anywhere in the design: the brand rejects a peak summer holiday treatment (which would oversell blue water and hard sun).

A warm, low-light grade is allowed, but after any warm move the line between sea and sky stays visible in cape_marren_member_harbour_seafood.jpg, cape_marren_member_oyster_landing.jpg and cape_marren_member_point_light.jpg; no grey sea is pushed toward blue, no sky is replaced or invented, and no photograph is desaturated or toned closer to monochrome than its source file; the brand rejects a 1,500 dollar luxury coastal weekend (which would go near monochrome and strand the bakery and the cider barn). A frame supplied grey, as those three are, stays honestly grey.

Task name: Palewell Health - Licensed care image campaign
Tagline: Care that meets you at home
Sector: Direct to consumer digital health platform with a growing employer benefits channel, sold to members and to the benefits leads who choose on their behalf
Founded / place / size: Founded 2019 in Portland, Oregon; an eleven person team, clinician led, still owner run
About: Palewell is a subscription digital health platform for people managing ordinary, everyday conditions from home. Members pay a modest monthly fee for clinician backed guidance, and about half our growth now comes through employer benefits teams who offer us to their staff. We exist so that steady, unglamorous care feels reachable rather than clinical.
Audience: Members aged thirty to fifty five who want reassurance without a hospital, plus benefits and HR leads who evaluate us for risk and coverage before putting us in front of their people
Price positioning: Fifteen to forty dollars a month, plus employer plans. Mid market and accessible: above a free wellness app, well below concierge medicine. The read must never feel like a two hundred dollar boutique practice or a supplement funnel.
Personality: calm, credible, human, steady, plainspoken, warm
Palette:
Deep Slate #2C3742 · mandatory. Our ground: the ground of the header, where the clinical lead sits on it (palewell_brand_notes.md), and any solid panel behind a photograph, as the photograph panel on palewell_employer_onepager.pdf. Also headlines, names and the contact block set on Warm Chalk or Paper White, as the brand line, name and contact on palewell_employer_onepager.pdf.
Warm Chalk #F3EEE6 · mandatory as the page ground of the poster and the referral panel. The ground for pages and space (palewell_brand_notes.md), as the page ground of palewell_employer_onepager.pdf; also type set on Deep Slate.
Sage Signal #6E8F7C · optional accent. The one accent, used sparingly: a link, a short rule or a small label, as the rule, plan tier line, small tagline label and contact label on palewell_employer_onepager.pdf. Never a ground, a panel, a headline or body text.
Soft Ink #4A5560 · mandatory where body text sits on Warm Chalk or Paper White. Body text and fine print set on Warm Chalk or Paper White (palewell_brand_notes.md), apart from a Sage Signal link or small label, as the body paragraph and footer line on palewell_employer_onepager.pdf. Never a ground or a panel, and never type on Deep Slate.
Paper White #FBFAF7 · optional. A near-white for a small panel or card on Warm Chalk, or for type set on Deep Slate. Never the page ground of the poster or the referral panel in place of Warm Chalk.
Typography: Palewell Health runs four steps. Step 01, Display and H1, is Archivo Black at 120 pt on 112 pt leading, tracked -15 thousandths, never more than four words, sitting at six times the body size with Inter beginning immediately beneath it. Step 02, Subheading and H2, is Archivo Black at 72 px on 76 px, tracked -10 thousandths, for the website header, with the referral panel stepping down to 48 px on 54 px. Step 03, Body, is Inter Regular at 18 px on 28 px, tracking 0, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, or 12 pt on 17 pt in print, and it is the body the headline is measured against. Voice: Plain, warm and unhurried; we speak to a person, not a patient. We avoid hype, superlatives and clinical jargon. Example line the brand would write: "Manage the everyday stuff with someone in your corner, from home."
Values: Credibility and warmth held together: real people in real rooms, honest about what we are, calm enough that a benefits lead trusts us with their staff.
Brand assets status: There is no formal brand book. What exists is an internal notes file describing the palette in words (a deep slate, a warm chalk, a single muted signal colour), the tone of voice, and what the founders mean by calm. We have never run a photo shoot: every image on the current site came free with the template, and we own exactly one photograph outright, of our clinical lead, cleared for use.

The poster and the referral panel sit on a Warm Chalk page ground, as palewell_employer_onepager.pdf does, and may carry solid Deep Slate panels, as that page's photograph panel, and small Paper White panels or cards. On Warm Chalk or Paper White, headlines, names and the contact block are Deep Slate, and body text and other fine print are Soft Ink, apart from a Sage Signal link or small label, as on palewell_employer_onepager.pdf. Task name: Cedar Commons - Farmers market identity restoration
Sector: A volunteer-run weekend farmers market in a municipal park, free to the public, funded by daily stall fees.
Founded / place / size: Founded 2016, in a park in Burlington, Vermont. Volunteer-run, 36 to 44 stalls, open weekends May through October.
About: Cedar Commons is a neighbourhood farmers market that runs on weekends in a Burlington park, free to walk into and funded entirely by the vendors who pay a daily stall fee. It has outgrown its chalkboards and its bedsheet banner. The signage exists to get families to the right lot, past the entrance and to the stall they are looking for, printed cheaply and well at a local sign shop.
Audience: Neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who arrive on foot or park in the wrong lot, plus the vendors and volunteers who run the morning. Read from a moving car and from across a field.
Price positioning: A free public market funded by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, often part-donated. Everything prints on coroplast and vinyl at a local sign shop. Flat inks and heavy type, never a refined tint palette that would be unreadable outdoors and would make a free market look like it is charging.
Personality: cheerful, practical, neighbourly, legible, unpretentious, outdoorsy
Palette:
Meadow Green #3F7D44 · mandatory wherever the stacked wordmark is set, and on every stall sign. CEDAR and COMMONS in the stacked wordmark, the green double square of the signature move; the trader name and the rule on every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf; other type on Sign White; a solid panel carrying Sign White type; or the single ink of the recovered mark.
Barn Red #B23A2E · mandatory wherever the stacked wordmark is set. The 10 mm rule the stacked wordmark sits on. Otherwise only small accents such as arrows; never a ground, a panel or body text.
Harvest Gold #E0A526 · optional accent. Small accents only, such as an arrow or a dot. Never a ground, a panel or type on Sign White: signage is read from a moving car and from across a field.
Sign White #FBFAF5 · mandatory ground on every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf; the ground behind the stacked wordmark wherever it is set. The ground of every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf, and the ground the stacked wordmark sits on; type reversed out of a Meadow Green or Cedar Ink panel. Not used in market-mark.svg, whose background stays transparent.
Cedar Ink #23301F · mandatory for the stall number on every stall sign. The stall number on every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf; dates, directions, listings and fine print on Sign White; a solid panel carrying Sign White type; or the single ink of the recovered mark.
Typography: Cedar Commons runs on two families. The name is Bodoni Egyptian Bold at 180 pt on 190 pt for a poster, stacked CEDAR above COMMONS, each line tracked out individually until the two measure exactly the same width, and the whole block set on a 10 mm Barn Red rule; the same lockup drops to 96 pt on 104 pt for a stall trader and 56 px on 60 px on screen, and it is never set on one line. Wayfinding is Interstate Bold at 60 pt on 66 pt, tracking +0.01 em. Listings and board copy are Interstate Regular at 18 pt on 24 pt, tracking 0, held to 65 characters a line. Fine print is Interstate Regular at 12 pt on 16 pt, tracking +0.03 em, and nothing sets smaller than that outdoors. Flat inks throughout, no tints.
Signature type move: The wordmark is always stacked, CEDAR above COMMONS, both lines tracked until they measure exactly the same width and set on a 10 mm Barn Red rule, so it reads as a green double square underlined in red before it reads as words.
Voice: Warm, plain and welcoming, like a volunteer at the gate. Example line: "Cheerful, legible from a distance, few colours, and it lives outdoors in the rain. Not precious. Tell us what our mark can and cannot do."
Values: Community and thrift. Recover the real mark rather than replace it, keep the set to a few flat inks that print cheaply, and tell the committee what the mark can and cannot do before they pay for plates.
Brand assets status: The market mark was drawn nine years ago by a volunteer's cousin, who is not reachable, and screen-printed onto aprons and tote bags. No file of any kind was ever kept. The stacked CEDAR COMMONS wordmark is Meadow Green on a Sign White ground, on its 10 mm Barn Red rule. Other type on Sign White is Cedar Ink or Meadow Green. No scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph.
Forbidden: No refined tint palette and no tint or screen of any ink; no metallic, foil or gloss effect, Harvest Gold included, which prints as a flat ink; no Harvest Gold type on Sign White. No colour outside the five palette hexes, #3F7D44, #B23A2E, #E0A526, #FBFAF5 and #23301F, for type, grounds, panels, rules, arrows, icons or the recovered mark.

Step 04, fine print, is Aktiv Grotesk Regular at 30 px on 38 px with tracking of plus 40 units for the ticket line and address. The printed lineup card sets the event line at 40 pt on a layout that never changes. The painted wall mark is never re-typeset.
Signature type move: The event line is blown up until the hairlines almost vanish and it runs off both edges, so the trim crops the letters rather than the type fitting the frame.
Voice: Direct and hyped but never fake, written the way the crew actually talks. Example line: 'Saturday. Warehouse. Tickets Tuesday. Do not sleep on it.'
Values: It belongs to the crowd: made by the people who run the night, not bought in.
Brand assets status: Pulsevault has never had a logo file. The mark exists only hand painted on the brick beside the entrance and survives as one photograph taken at the end of the night under a single floodlight. The wordmark has to be recovered from that photograph as artwork the night can reuse, and it has to hold on a cover that is close to black. There is no colour spec and no prior guideline. The one thing the night reprints unchanged is a plain lineup card its print shop runs a small batch of each month, supplied as last month's flat press artwork: the running order and the per act details change every date, the layout does not.
Palette rules:
Distribution: Blackout is the only ground: the cover, the next-event announcement and every title or closing card in the films sit on Blackout, as pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf does, and a photograph or footage may sit on it, screened darker with Blackout behind type. On Blackout, the event line and act names are the warm off-white #F2ECE0 of the card's masthead and act name; the date, ticket, doors, door and age lines are warm off-white, Laser Cyan or Concrete; slot numbers may be Laser Cyan and set times Concrete, as on the card. Stage Magenta fills the event line's counters and small chips carrying light type (#F7EEF4 on the card's billing pill). Laser Cyan, Flood Amber and Concrete together cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground or panel; Flood Amber is never type.
Opacity: Every palette colour, and the card's warm off-white, is used solid at 100% opacity on type, chips, panels and rules, with no tint, transparency, gradient, glow or blend mode. The one overlay allowed is the one pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf uses, which screens its full-bleed floor still dark behind the type: a photograph or footage may be screened darker with Blackout #0C0C0F alone, which darkens it without changing its hues. No overlay, wash or gradient of any other colour, white included, is laid over a photograph or footage. A card or line may cut or fade in or out as a whole; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
Forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, chips, panels, rules or icons, except the warm off-white of pulsevault_lineup_card_press.pdf (#F2ECE0, and #F7EEF4 in its billing pill) and the painted wordmark's own paint as recovered from pulsevault_wall_mark.jpg. No light or white ground. No glow, gloss, bevel, chrome, metallic or 3D effect on any type, chip, rule or the wordmark, since nothing may read as agency polish.
Photography: Footage and stills keep their own recorded light and colour and are never tinted or recoloured toward the palette. A picture may be screened darker with Blackout behind type; nothing else is laid over it, and no crowd, room or light is generated, extended or replaced.

Task name: Velvet Hour - Social film and story cutdowns
Tagline: One night a month, sit down and listen.
Sector: Arts, culture and live music (monthly ticketed jazz and folk night)
Founded / place / size: Founded 2021 in the back room of a bar, Providence, Rhode Island. Tiny: two organisers, ninety seats, one night a month.
About: Velvet Hour is a monthly ticketed jazz and folk night held in the ninety seat back room of a Providence bar. Two sets, no support, one camera in the same corner every month. The night sells intimacy and musicianship to people who read a lineup carefully, so everything we make should feel like a good room rather than a club or a concert hall.
Audience: Lineup literate adults roughly thirty to sixty who pay eighteen to twenty five dollars to sit close and listen. Locals who follow the acts, not a party crowd.
Price positioning: Mid, intimate. An eighteen to twenty five dollar ticket. Never budget club, never black tie concert hall.
Personality: Warm, Unhurried, Intimate, Editorial, Understated
Palette:
Lamp Cream #EFE3C8 · mandatory. Every act name, the venue name, billing, door time, price and body type set on Back Room Green or over footage, as on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf; the one ink of the moth and lamp mark, as painted on velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg; and the ground of a small-print strip, as the footer strip of velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf.
Back Room Green #243026 · mandatory. The main ground: the poster ground, the film end card and any solid panel, as the card ground of velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf and the board the mark is painted on in velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg. Not a type colour.
Warm Ink #1C1A17 · mandatory where type sits on Lamp Cream. Small print and all type on a Lamp Cream ground, as the footer paragraph of velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf, and the plain well behind a photograph, as its photo well. Never type on Back Room Green.
Ember Amber #C8873F · optional accent. Hairline rules and the date line, as the rule above the act name and the date on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf. Always flat. Never a ground, a panel or an act name.
Dust Rose #B6837C · optional accent. The tagline “One night a month, sit down and listen.” only, set small, as the kicker line on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf. Never a ground, a panel or an act name.
Typography: Velvet Hour runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Adobe Caslon Pro Regular 400 at 96 pt on 104 pt leading, tracking minus 5 units on the given name and 120 units on the true small caps surname: the headline act stacked on two lines, given name above surname, so the second line falls quieter than the first. Step 02, subheading, is the same face and stack at 48 pt on 54 pt for support acts, tracking minus 3 units on the given name and 120 units on the small caps surname, with the date line beneath at 24 pt on 30 pt in National 2 Regular. Step 03, body, is National 2 Regular at 11 pt on 16 pt, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters, with the ticket line in National 2 Medium at the same size. Step 04, fine print, is National 2 Regular at 8 pt on 12 pt with tracking of plus 25 units. The film title card carries the same two line stack at 54 px on 64 px. An act name is never set in the sans.
Signature type move: Every act name stacks on two lines, given name above surname, with the surname in true Caslon small caps tracked 120 units so the second line falls quieter than the first.
Voice: Plain, affectionate, low key. Talks about the room and the players, never hypes. Short sentences, no exclamation, lets the act's face and the music do the work.
Values: Story first, no gimmicks. Clean, coherent, honest to the room. We would rather look like a place people sit and listen than like a night that is trying too hard.
Brand assets status: Our mark, a moth over a lamp inside a hairline arc of small caps type, was made by the designer who set up the night, and the source file went with them when they left. All that survives is the mark painted in one cream ink on the dark green lamp box by the door, which is why it has to be rebuilt from that as real artwork. No brand typeface was ever formally chosen, so the type system is open for you to set.
Palette rules:
Distribution: Back Room Green is the main ground for the poster, the film end card and any solid panel, as on velvet_hour_listing_card_printer.pdf. Lamp Cream is a ground only for a small-print strip, where all type is Warm Ink, as that card's footer. On Back Room Green and over footage, act names, the venue name, billing, door time, price and body are Lamp Cream; the date line may be Ember Amber and the tagline Dust Rose, as on the card. The mark is drawn in flat Lamp Cream on Back Room Green, as painted on velvet_hour_lampbox.jpg. Ember Amber and Dust Rose are accents for hairline rules, the date line and the tagline only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground, a panel or an act name.
Opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, any type or the mark, and no scrim, vignette, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage or a photograph: type sits straight on the footage or on a solid Back Room Green card or panel. In the films a card or line may cut or fade in and out as a whole; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
Forbidden: No gold, foil, metallic sheen, glow, drop shadow or other display gimmick on any type, rule, panel or the mark, as the brand's own typography note rules out (“No display gimmicks, no gold foil gestures.”); Ember Amber is always a flat colour. No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, grounds, panels, rules or the mark.
Photography: Footage and photographs keep their own colour and are never tinted, duotoned or washed toward the palette. The six takes keep the warm lamp light and the green room as filmed. The act photographs keep natural skin: next_month_act_01.jpg is not pushed grey or orange, and the printed halftone dots in next_month_act_04.jpg are not resampled into a moire. A bar still such as velvet_hour_still_07.jpg keeps natural skin under its warm cast, not taken grey by a whole-frame neutral balance.

Task name: Milepost Driving Academy - Scenario clip training library
Sector: Driver education and road safety training (accredited in car and classroom academy)
Founded / place / size: Established 2009 in Burlington, Vermont. Small: two instructors, roughly sixty learners a term.
About: Milepost is an accredited driving academy in Vermont running in car lessons and a classroom course. Two instructors, about sixty learners a term, mostly sixteen to nineteen with a steady number of adult beginners. Our reputation is that we are calm and thorough, and every learner leaves certain about what they are looking at. Everything we make has to earn the trust of a nervous learner and the parent paying for the course.
Audience: Learners sixteen to nineteen plus adult beginners, with the purchase decision usually made by a parent. People who want reassurance that the school is careful and legitimate.
Price positioning: Mid, accredited and dependable. Sixty dollars an hour. Not a budget app, not a premium driving experience brand.
Personality: Calm, Thorough, Clear, Accountable, Neutral
Palette:
Signal Green #2E6B4F · mandatory. The scenario number, with its 3 px Caution Amber rule beneath (type system signature move), and the scenario title, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf, always on Route White. Never a ground, a panel, step text or callout text.
Route White #F7F7F4 · mandatory. The only ground: every text card and text panel, as the page ground of milepost_guide_2019.pdf. All type sits on it, never directly on road footage.
Slate Text #2A2E33 · mandatory where steps, the callout or captions sit on Route White. Step lines, the callout and captions on Route White, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf, and the stop glyph, drawn like the single dark ink of milepost_glyph_sheet.jpg. Never a ground or panel.
Caution Amber #E4A11B · mandatory as the 3 px rule beneath every scenario number. Thin rules only: the 3 px rule directly beneath the scenario number, and at most a short rule above the callout, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf. Never type, a ground, a panel or a fill.
Sky Grey #9AA6AE · optional accent. A footer or accreditation line and hairline rules only, as the footer of milepost_guide_2019.pdf. Never a ground, a panel, step text or callout text.
Typography: Milepost runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Baskerville Display PT Regular at 72 px on 80 px leading with tracking of minus 10 units for the scenario title, and the scenario number sets in the same face at three times that size, 216 px, in Signal Green with a 3 px Caution Amber rule directly beneath it. The vertical cutdown title runs 64 px on 72 px, and the school name is the only other Baskerville setting, in Bold. Step 02, subheading, is Inter Semibold at 56 px on 64 px with tracking of minus 5 units for callouts, because Baskerville is reserved for the school name and scenario titles. Step 03, body, is Inter Regular at 44 px on 58 px, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters. Step 04, fine print, is Inter Regular at 32 px on 42 px with tracking of plus 20 units for captions and the accreditation line. Inter carries tabular lining figures at every size, the printed guide sets body at 11 pt on 16 pt, and a step is never set in italic or caps.
Signature type move: Every scenario carries its number set in Baskerville Display PT at three times the title size, in Signal Green, with a 3 px Caution Amber rule directly beneath it.
Voice: Calm, instructive, reassuring. One idea at a time, numbered where it helps, no slang and no drama. Speaks plainly to a beginner and to the parent reading over their shoulder.
Values: Certainty over style. A learner and a parent must always be sure what they are looking at. Nothing stylised, nothing that reads as styling over substance, consistency that shows the school is careful.
Brand assets status: Everything a learner currently sees from us dates to 2019 and looks it. The printer holds the press file for the guide, but the source files for our simplified sign shapes are gone: they only survive as a photograph of a sheet our first designer printed and taped to the wall, so those glyphs have to be recovered from that. No brand typeface was ever locked, so the type system is open for you to set to our legibility standard.
Palette rules:
Distribution: Route White is the only ground: the scenario number, title, steps and callout sit on a solid Route White card or panel, never directly on road footage, as milepost_guide_2019.pdf keeps its type off the photograph. On Route White, the scenario number and scenario title are Signal Green, and step lines, the callout and captions are Slate Text, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf. Caution Amber is for thin rules only and Sky Grey for a footer or accreditation line and hairlines only; together they take no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground, a panel, step text or callout text.
Opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity, once a card or panel is fully on screen. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over the road footage: text sits on a solid Route White card or panel.
Forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules or glyphs, so no red stop sign glyph, and no gradient, glow, outline, drop shadow or metallic effect on any type, panel, rule or glyph: nothing is stylised.
Photography: Road footage and road stills keep their own filmed colour and are never tinted or graded toward the palette. The warm low-sun cast of milepost_road_still_01.jpg and milepost_road_still_02.jpg is not pushed toward Caution Amber, the cool fog of milepost_road_still_03.jpg and milepost_road_still_04.jpg is not pushed toward Sky Grey, and the painted road markings in every take keep the colours they were filmed in.

Task name: FOLD & GRAIN Studio - Dual-client sizzle and service package
Tagline: One take. Everything you need to sell it.
Sector: Product photography studio moving from a day rate practice to a fixed price productized service
Founded / place / size: Founded 2020 in Portland, Oregon. Three people: Nina (art direction and shooting), plus a retoucher and a studio assistant.
About: FOLD & GRAIN shoots small brands' products the way those brands actually sell them, in a row, as a range, rather than one hero at a time. For six years we sold days. We are now selling a product: one continuous take per client and, out of that single take, the shot board, the short films and the platform cuts a small brand needs to launch. Our work sits behind pantry goods at eight dollars and sterling silver at a hundred and eighty, and the whole point is that the same method tunes to each. Precision, repeatability and honesty about what a shoot can and cannot yield are the studio's stock in trade.
Audience: Small and independent product brands (pantry, personal care, jewellery, homeware) launching or refreshing a web store and needing a full range shot to look like one afternoon. Founders who buy a fixed price and a fixed turnaround, not a day rate.
Price positioning: Repositioning from roughly fifteen hundred dollars a day to a fixed twenty two hundred to thirty five hundred dollars per client run. Mid-market, productized, premium to a freelancer but well under an agency.
Personality: Exacting, Plainspoken, Craft-first, Unfussy, Quietly confident
Palette:
Paper White #F5F1E8 · mandatory. The ground of every Cobbleway Provisions board page and of any card or panel carrying Cobbleway Provisions material, as the pale warm sweep the Cobbleway pass was shot on; and the colour of type set on Ink Black or on the dark Lunara Silver footage, apart from Slate Grey mono specs and Lunara prices.
Ink Black #1A1A17 · mandatory. Type on Paper White or on the pale Cobbleway Provisions footage: headings, body, captions, prices and the FOLD & GRAIN wordmark, apart from Slate Grey mono specs and Kraft Tan small labels; and the ground of every Lunara Silver board page and of any card or panel carrying Lunara Silver material, as the dark slab the Lunara pass was shot on.
Kraft Tan #C7A879 · optional accent, Cobbleway Provisions material only. Hairline rules, dividers and small labels on Cobbleway Provisions deliverables and the Cobbleway example of the service page, echoing the kraft cartons. Never a ground, card, panel, heading, body text or price, and never in Lunara Silver material.
Slate Grey #6D7378 · optional accent. Sohne Mono Buch specs and parameters on either ground, Lunara Silver prices, which the approved copy asks to be understated, and hairline rules and dividers. Never a ground, card, panel, heading, body text or the wordmark.
Typography: FOLD & GRAIN runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Engravers LT Std Bold Face, caps only, at 72 px on 78 px leading with tracking of plus 60 units for the service page headline, and 180 units on the stacked wordmark, which always sets FOLD above GRAIN with the ampersand small and centred between them. Because Engravers is a caps only face, display tracking opens rather than tightens. Step 02, subheading, is the same face at 34 px on 40 px with tracking of plus 90 units for section and board headings; no size existed for this role, so it is set proportionate to the 72 px headline and the 28 pt printed board title. Step 03, body, is Neue Haas Grotesk Text 55 Roman at 18 px on 28 px, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters. Step 04, fine print, is Sohne Mono Buch at 14 px on 20 px with tracking of plus 15 units, carrying specs, parameters and prices in tabular figures. In print the board title runs 28 pt, captions and prices 12 pt and mono specs 8 pt on 12 pt. The wordmark is never set in the mono.
Signature type move: The wordmark always stacks on two lines, FOLD above GRAIN with the ampersand set small and centred between them, tracked 180 units so it reads as a struck stamp rather than a line of type.
Voice: Direct, specific, no salesmanship. We name what a shoot can deliver and what it cannot, and we write our recipes so an assistant could run them. Sentences are short and concrete.
Values: Repeatability over one-off flourish, honesty about limits, and price-appropriate craft: a treatment right for one band is wrong for another, and saying so is the service.
Brand assets status: FOLD & GRAIN has a consistent working look built up over six years but never a codified system. There is a set wordmark and studio colours in practice, no written guidelines. This engagement, which includes the studio's own service page, is where the identity gets formalized for the first time.
Palette rules:
Distribution: Grounds, cards and panels are Paper White or Ink Black and nothing else. Cobbleway Provisions material sits on Paper White, as the pale warm sweep it was shot on; Lunara Silver material sits on Ink Black, as its dark slab. On Paper White or the pale Cobbleway footage, type is Ink Black; on Ink Black or the dark Lunara footage, type is Paper White. Slate Grey may carry mono specs and parameters on either ground and Lunara prices; Kraft Tan may carry hairline rules, dividers and small labels in Cobbleway material only. The two accents together take no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground, card or panel.
Opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour or type, and no scrim, gradient, vignette or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage or a photograph: type sits directly on the picture or on a solid palette card or panel. A fade in or out of a whole shot or card at a film transition is allowed.
Forbidden: No colour outside the four palette hexes (#F5F1E8, #1A1A17, #C7A879 and #6D7378) for type, cards, panels, rules, icons or the FOLD & GRAIN wordmark, and no Kraft Tan anywhere in Lunara Silver material.
Photography: Footage and frame grabs are never tinted, duotoned or washed toward a palette colour, and the palette rules above do not apply to their pixels. The Cobbleway Provisions sweep is not pushed toward Kraft Tan or orange; the Lunara Silver slab keeps its own dark stone texture, is not flattened to Ink Black, and the silver is not warmed.
